title: Protein Secondary Structure Visualization with Undo/Redo
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that visualizes protein secondary structure elements (alpha-helices, beta-sheets, and random coils) in an interactive 3D scene with full undo/redo support.

## Scene Setup
- Black background, perspective camera at position (0, 5, 25), looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404040, intensity 0.5) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 1.0) at (10, 15, 10).
- OrbitControls for camera rotation/zoom.
- The protein backbone is a chain of 30 residues laid out along the X-axis, each residue represented by a small sphere (radius 0.2) at positions spaced 1.0 unit apart, centered around origin (i.e., x from -14.5 to +14.5).

## Secondary Structure Types
Each residue has a secondary structure assignment: 'helix', 'sheet', or 'coil'.
- Initial assignment: residues 0-7 = 'helix', 8-13 = 'sheet', 14-19 = 'coil', 20-25 = 'helix', 26-29 = 'sheet'.
- Helix residues: colored red (0xff3333), rendered with a helical ribbon tube (CylinderGeometry or TubeGeometry) connecting them, radius 0.6.
- Sheet residues: colored yellow (0xffdd33), rendered with flat arrow-like boxes (BoxGeometry, height 0.15, width 1.2) connecting them.
- Coil residues: colored gray (0x999999), rendered with thin tube connections (radius 0.15).
- Backbone spheres are always visible and colored according to their current type.

## Residue Selection & Reassignment
- Clicking on a residue sphere selects it (outline it with a wireframe sphere, color cyan 0x00ffff). Store selectedResidueIndex in state.
- Only one residue selected at a time. Clicking empty space deselects.
- Three DOM buttons labeled 'Assign Helix', 'Assign Sheet', 'Assign Coil' in a top-right panel.
- Clicking a button reassigns the selected residue's secondary structure type, updates its color and the connecting geometry, and pushes the action onto the undo stack.
- Keyboard shortcut 'H' assigns helix, 'S' assigns sheet, 'C' assigns coil to selected residue.

## Undo/Redo System
- Maintain an undoStack and redoStack of actions. Each action records {residueIndex, oldType, newType}.
- Ctrl+Z triggers undo: pop from undoStack, revert the residue, push to redoStack.
- Ctrl+Y triggers redo: pop from redoStack, reapply, push to undoStack.
- DOM buttons 'Undo' and 'Redo' in a top-left panel also trigger these.
- Max undo stack depth: 50 actions.

## Statistics HUD
- A DOM overlay at bottom-center showing: 'Helices: N | Sheets: M | Coils: K | Total: 30'.
- These counts must always sum to 30 (conservation law).
- Update counts after every assignment, undo, or redo.

## Highlight Mode Toggle
- Pressing 'T' toggles highlight mode. In highlight mode, all residues not matching the most common secondary structure type become semi-transparent (opacity 0.3). The most common type stays fully opaque.
- Pressing 'T' again restores all to full opacity.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- residues: array of 30 objects, each {index, type: 'helix'|'sheet'|'coil', x, y, z}
- selectedResidueIndex: number or -1 if none selected
- undoStackSize: number
- redoStackSize: number
- helixCount: number
- sheetCount: number
- coilCount: number
- totalCount: 30 (always)
- highlightMode: boolean
- lastAction: {type: 'assign'|'undo'|'redo'|'select'|'deselect'|'toggleHighlight', detail: object} or null
- cameraPosition: {x, y, z}
- sceneReady: boolean (true after init)

Update __3D_STATE__ synchronously after every interaction.
physics_constraints: Conservation law: helixCount + sheetCount + coilCount must always equal 30. Undo must perfectly restore previous state. Redo must perfectly restore the undone action. No residue may have an undefined or invalid type. All residue positions must be NaN-free. The undo/redo stacks must be consistent: performing undo then redo returns to the same state.
